scope: section 42 item 11 and section 9: the first version does registry, enable, disable, health, default, fallback, rollback and permission, and does not do a public marketplace.
what_a_capability_record_must_carry: health state and when it was last checked
fallback provider if this one fails
permission or scope it runs under
the media types it accepts and the outputs it produces
already_implemented_in_the_core: capability routes are declared at launch rather than inferred from the checkout layout
the Core registers exactly what was declared (Executor::open_routes)
a worker identity allow-list refuses an unexpected worker before it serves anything
the receipt names the engine and engine_version that produced a result
not_yet_implemented: provider rollback, beyond naming the fallback candidate
a second provider for any capability in a production launch, which is why fallback reads null there even though the field and its behaviour are tested
permission or scope per capability; the launch token model remains the only gate

provider_catalogue_measured_on_this_host.note: the model runtime is installed and serving; this records what a registry would have to describe, not a claim that the registry exists
provider_catalogue_measured_on_this_host.vision_caption: wired through a capability route and measured producing a real caption
provider_catalogue_measured_on_this_host.h3_video: the ComfyUI runtime resolves all three H3 component classes; no route exists

invariant: a capability provider never writes the canonical database; it answers a bounded request and the Core validates and commits the result

implemented_over_http.GET /api/v1/capabilities: the routes the Core registered, each with provider, health, enabled, is_default and fallback
implemented_over_http.GET /api/v1/capabilities/{capability}: one capability by exact dot-separated name; a near miss is 404 rather than the nearest match
implemented_over_http.PUT /api/v1/capabilities/{capability}/en: enable/disable, persisted in capability_settings and answered from the re-read record rather than echoed back

enforcement_note: Disable is a real barrier, not a report: `attempts::claim` reads the record inside the claim transaction, so a disabled capability creates no attempt row, no staging copy and no partial output, and the execute path answers 409 AAK-CAP-001 before the worker starts. A check placed after the worker started would make 'disabled' mean 'ran and was then discarded'.
schema_note: capability_settings arrived with schema version 7 and is in the archive export table set, so a backup/restore round trip keeps it rather than silently dropping which capabilities an operator turned off.

recorded_over.delivered: the registry surface and its limits
enable/disable persisted, refused at claim time
default and fallback reporting, preferring a usable provider
